featured_reviews.name: Enal Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Definitely worth Visiting!!!!!!

I tried their breakfast combo, which cost me ₹131 after applying GST.

My first impression was that it was such a small quantity that it wouldn't even fill the stomach of a single person. However, as soon as I started eating, I was pleasantly surprised.

1) The quality - It was the best I've had, and I didn't regret paying for it. It was really nice.

2) Taste - It had a homely taste. Yes, they do take time to serve you because everything is prepared freshly, but the taste is really nice. 3) Quantity - No matter how it looks on the plate, it's enough for an average healthy person. I was on an empty stomach when I had it, and it made me so full that I had my evening snack directly after breakfast.

4) Location - It's in the heart of Mumbai, near the railway station, and the location and ambiance are just too good.

5) Price range - Being in South Mumbai, in a prime location, what they are offering at this price is just awesome. Except for the buffet, other dishes on the menu are reasonably priced.

Conclusion: GO FOR IT. I am eager to go again. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sri Krishna Restaurant is a place I’ve visited a few times over the years, and it continues to be a dependable option in the Mumbai dining scene, especially for South Indian vegetarian food.

One of the standout items here, in my experience, is the Dahi Vada, which I’ve had on multiple occasions and would definitely recommend. It’s consistently well-prepared and enjoyable.

On my most recent order, I also tried the Medu Vada and Rava Masala Dosa. While the food overall was good, I wasn’t particularly impressed with the sambar that accompanied the vada. Since sambar plays a key role in the dish, this did affect the overall experience for me. The rest of the preparation, however, was satisfactory.

They also offer a variety of ice creams, and the mango option we tried was quite good and made for a nice finish to the meal.

Service here is excellent. The staff are attentive and helpful, with waiters proactively suggesting dishes and offering recommendations in a thoughtful, non-pushy manner and something that enhances the overall dining experience.

The restaurant is purely vegetarian and has a cool, calm, comfortable ambience, making it suitable for a quiet, relaxed lunch or dinner.

Overall, Sri Krishna remains a reliable and recommended spot, particularly for its strengths in select dishes and service.

featured_reviews.name: Suraj Powar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Really horrible experience. From the moment we arrived, the service was dishonest and unacceptable. We requested seating in the air-conditioned section, but both the waiter and the manager told us that the AC section was closed to the public. Since the non-AC area was completely packed except for one table, we considered leaving. Only then did the manager suddenly suggest we go upstairs—where we clearly saw a group of around 11 people already having their lunch. This made it obvious that we were misled from the start.
The situation only worsened. Plates were placed on our table before the food arrived, and they were visibly dirty. I had to explicitly request a clean plate. Even the replacement plate, which is attached in the photos, was far from acceptable. This level of hygiene is absolutely disgusting and completely unacceptable for any restaurant.
To make matters worse, our bill was incorrect, adding yet another layer of frustration. The food itself was mediocre at best—certainly not good enough to justify the poor service and lack of basic standards.
I was extremely disappointed and upset by the entire experience. A restaurant should treat all customers equally and with respect, which clearly did not happen here. I will never return and do not recommend this place to anyone

featured_reviews.name: Amrutjyoti Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text: Heard a lot about this place from reels, and was not disappointed. Went with 3 friends around 3:30 pm on 14th Feb. It was not crowded at all. Started with the Iced Filter Coffee, was a little watered down, but you can always ask for more coffee concoction. Then the Goli Bhaji and Mangalore Buns were absolutely delicious, not too sweet, perfectly balancing the sweetness with the coconut chutney. Then we got 4 different doses, and the Ghee Podi Benne Masala Dosa (jain) was the bestseller for a reason. First bite was heavenly and comforting, and the masala was made of raw banana, and was in sufficient quantity. The dosa was only so flavorful, there was no need of sambar or chutney. If you take regular dosa, you get an additional tomato garlic chutney. My friend ordered the Mulbagal Dosa, which they claim to have started the 1st time in Mumbai. Some might say you would get doses at cheaper prices elsewhere, but their price reflects their commitment to perfection and love towards serving people. I will definitely visit this place again..!!

featured_reviews.name: Aditya Gujar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Shiv Sagar near Mumbai Central Station, and it was a great experience for anyone looking for flavorful vegetarian food. This place is a well-known spot for North and South Indian cuisine, serving quality food with a quick service time.

We ordered Veg Kolhapuri, Roti, and Jeera Rice. The Veg Kolhapuri was perfectly spiced, with a rich, thick gravy loaded with fresh vegetables. The spice level was just right—not too mild, not overly spicy—giving it an authentic Kolhapuri taste. The rotis were soft, freshly made, and paired well with the curry. The Jeera Rice was well-cooked, aromatic, and light, making for a great combination with the sabzi.

The restaurant was clean and well-maintained, with a simple but comfortable dining setup. Since it’s near Mumbai Central, it gets quite busy, but the service was decent quick and efficient. The staff were polite and ensured we had a smooth dining experience.

The pricing is quite high, and the portion sizes are satisfying. Whether you’re travelling through Mumbai Central or looking for a good vegetarian meal in the area, Shiv Sagar is definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Akhil Vishnu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kanishka Veg Restaurant is a prominent pure vegetarian eatery situated in Mumbai, strategically located near iconic landmarks like the Mahalakshmi Temple and Haji Ali Dargah, making it a convenient dining spot for visitors exploring these spiritual sites. Nestled at 5-B, Haji Ali Circle, Tardeo Road, Mahalaxmi, the restaurant offers an inviting ambiance conducive for family dinners and casual meals alike.¹

Kanishka Veg Restaurant serves an array of delectable vegetarian dishes catering to diverse palates. *Authentic South Indian dishes* like _Sada Dosa_ and _Rava Masala Dosa_ are highlights, delivering *typical South Indian taste* that's true to regional flavors, complemented by flavorful chutneys that enhance the culinary experience. Patrons praise the *tasty dosa*, underscoring the restaurant's knack for capturing traditional essence.² ³

The restaurant boasts a *good atmosphere*, with interiors that are well-furnished and equipped with pleasant lighting, fostering a comfortable dining environment. Reviews highlight *good service*, with staff often described as attentive, friendly, and polite – essential for patrons seeking hassle-free dining, even during bustling festival periods like Diwali and Raksha Bandhan.⁴

Among popular items, diners specifically love *paneer tikka*, *kulcha*, *cheese pulav*, and *fried rice*, showcasing the kitchen's versatility across North Indian and Chinese-inspired vegetarian preparations. *Pav Bhaji* is another crowd-pleaser, available with options like Jain Pav Bhaji, reflecting accommodation for diverse dietary preferences.

On the beverage front, while the *chocolate shake is average*, visitors appreciate refreshing options like lassi – with one reviewer finding the lassi "definitely worth trying – refreshing and delicious!".

Kanishka Veg Restaurant offers a balanced mix of affordability and quality, with price ranges typically ₹200-₹400 per person, making it accessible for varied budgets. Cuisines span *South Indian*, *North Indian*, *Chinese*, *Fast Food*, and vegetarian staples, appealing to those craving familiar comfort food with vegetarian integrity.

Located opposite Haji Ali Juice Centre, proximity to spiritual hubs like Mahalakshmi Temple (0.3 km from Baskin-Robbins, another nearby eatery) and Haji Ali Dargah positions Kanishka Veg Restaurant as a practical choice for visitors blending devotion with gastronomy. Other nearby dining options include Cafe Noorani, McDonald’s Tardeo, and Haji Ali Juice Centre for those exploring alternatives.⁵

Operating hours stretch from *8 AM to 12 AM*, accommodating breakfast through late-night cravings.
